title: Match the shaded region to an inequality
subtitle: Linear inequalities in one or two variables · 5 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **5 of the official questions in Linear inequalities in one or two variables are this one** — 2 Easy, 2 Medium, 1 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get an xy-plane with a boundary line (slanted or horizontal) and one side shaded.
- The question asks which inequality the region represents, or asks for a constant inside a given inequality whose graph is shown.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Read two lattice points on the boundary.
- Find the slope and the y-intercept, and write y = mx + b.
- For a horizontal line, write y = c.
- 2) Shading above the line means y > (or ≥); shading below means y <.
- A solid line includes the boundary, and a dashed line makes the inequality strict.
- 3) If the choices or the given inequality are in a different form, e.g. with a coefficient on y, rearrange.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Excellent.
Type each answer choice as an inequality and see which shading and line style match the picture.
For a hidden constant, use a slider on it until the boundary lines up.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You get the slope's sign wrong.
You pick 'greater than' vs 'less than' from the visual side without first rewriting the inequality as y alone, so a negative coefficient on y flips the meaning.
Or you mix up a solid line with a dashed one.

sections.heading: You are losing these
